title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Civil Dispute Cases Related to Enterprise Restructuring

articles.content_en: Article 2: Where a party initiates a prosecution that falls under the circumstances listed in Article 1 of these Provisions and satisfies the conditions for prosecution prescribed in Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall accept it.

Article 3: Where disputes arise during the administrative adjustment or transfer of state-owned assets of enterprises by the competent government departments, and a party brings a civil action to the People's Court, the People's Court shall not accept it.
II. Corporate System Reform of Enterprises

Article 4: Where a state-owned enterprise is wholly restructured into a wholly state-owned limited liability company in accordance with the Company Law, the debts of the original enterprise shall be borne by the restructured limited liability company.

Article 5: Where an enterprise, through increasing capital and expanding shares or transferring part of its property rights, enables others to take an equity stake in the enterprise and restructures the entire enterprise into a limited liability company or a joint stock limited company, the debts of the original enterprise shall be borne by the newly established company after the restructuring.

Article 6: Where an enterprise forms a new company with others using part of its property and corresponding debts, if the creditors approve the transferred debts, the newly formed company shall bear civil liability; if the creditors were not notified of the transferred debts, or although notified, the creditors do not approve, the original enterprise shall bear civil liability. Where the original enterprise is unable to repay its debts, and the creditors claim debts against the newly established company on this ground, the newly established company shall, within the scope of the property it received, bear joint and several civil liability with the original enterprise.

Article 7: Where an enterprise forms a new company with others using its high-quality property while leaving the debts with the original enterprise, and a creditor brings a lawsuit against the newly established company and the original enterprise as co-defendants to claim debts, the newly established company shall, within the scope of the property it received, bear joint and several liability together with the original enterprise.
III. Joint-Stock Cooperative System Reform of Enterprises

Article 8: Where the employees of an enterprise buy out the property rights of the enterprise and restructure the original enterprise into a joint-stock cooperative enterprise, the debts of the original enterprise shall be borne by the restructured joint-stock cooperative enterprise.

Article 9: Where an enterprise transfers part of its property rights to its employees, and the enterprise and the employees jointly form a joint-stock cooperative enterprise, the debts of the original enterprise shall be borne by the restructured joint-stock cooperative enterprise.

Article 10: Where an enterprise, through investment by its employees to increase capital and expand shares, restructures the original enterprise into a joint-stock cooperative enterprise, the debts of the original enterprise shall be borne by the restructured joint-stock cooperative enterprise.

Article 11: Where an enterprise, when conducting the joint-stock cooperative system reform, publicly notifies its creditors by reference to the relevant provisions of the Company Law. After the joint-stock cooperative system reform of the enterprise, if a creditor sues the joint-stock cooperative enterprise for debts concealed or omitted by the asset administrator (contributor) of the original enterprise, and if the creditor has reported the claim within the announcement period, the joint-stock cooperative enterprise may, after bearing civil liability, claim reimbursement from the asset administrator (contributor) of the original enterprise. If the creditor has not reported the claim within the announcement period, the joint-stock cooperative enterprise shall not bear civil liability, and the People's Court may inform the creditor to separately sue the asset administrator (contributor) of the original enterprise.
IV. Division of Enterprises

Article 12: Where a creditor claims debts against the enterprises after division, if there is an agreement on the assumption of the debts of the original enterprise at the time of division and the creditors approve it, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the agreement of the parties; if there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear on the assumption of the debts of the original enterprise at the time of division, or although there is an agreement, the creditors do not approve it, the enterprises after division shall bear joint and several liability.

Article 13: After the divided enterprises bear joint and several liability, if there is an agreement among the divided enterprises on the assumption of the debts of the original enterprise, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the agreement; if there is no agreement or the agreement is unclear, the debts shall be apportioned according to the asset ratio at the time of division.
V. Conversion of Enterprise Creditor's Rights into Equity

Article 14: Where a creditor and a debtor voluntarily reach an agreement on the conversion of creditor's rights into equity, and the agreement does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, the People's Court shall, when trying the relevant civil dispute case, confirm that the agreement on conversion of creditor's rights into equity is valid.
Policy-based conversion of creditor's rights into equity shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of the relevant departments of the State Council.

Article 15: Where a debtor, by concealing enterprise assets or falsely listing enterprise assets, induces a creditor to conclude an agreement on the conversion of creditor's rights into equity, and the creditor exercises the right of revocation within the statutory period, the People's Court shall support it.
After the agreement on conversion of creditor's rights into equity is revoked, the creditor has the right to require the debtor to pay off the debts.

Article 16: The act of some creditors converting creditor's rights into equity shall not affect the rights of other creditors to claim debts against the debtor.
VI. Sale of State-Owned Small Enterprises

Article 17: Where an enterprise is sold by agreement transfer, and the enterprise sale contract has not been approved by the local people's government with examination and approval authority or its authorized functional department, the People's Court shall, when trying the relevant civil dispute case, confirm that the enterprise sale contract has not taken effect.

Article 18: Where, in the sale of an enterprise, both parties maliciously collude to harm national interests, the People's Court shall, when trying the relevant civil dispute case, confirm that the sale of the enterprise is void.

Article 19: Where, in the sale of an enterprise, the act of the seller has the circumstances for revocation prescribed by law, and the buyer exercises the right of revocation within the statutory period, the People's Court shall support it.

Article 20: Where the performance period stipulated in the enterprise sale contract expires, and one party refuses to perform the contract, or fails to fully perform its contractual obligations, thereby making the purpose of the contract unattainable, and the other party requests dissolution of the contract and compensation for losses, the People's Court shall support it.

Article 21: Where the performance period stipulated in the enterprise sale contract expires, and one party fails to fully perform its contractual obligations, and the other party requests continued performance of the contract and compensation for losses, the People's Court shall support it. Where both parties fail to fully perform their contractual obligations, the civil liability to be borne by each party shall be determined according to the fault of the parties.

Article 22: Where, at the time of the sale of an enterprise, the seller fails to perform the obligation of truthful disclosure regarding material matters such as the assets and liabilities status and profit and loss status of the enterprise sold, thereby affecting the sale price, and the buyer brings a lawsuit to the People's Court claiming compensation on this ground, the People's Court shall support it.

Article 23: Where the enterprise sale contract is confirmed void or revoked, the operating profits and losses incurred during the buyer's operation of the enterprise after the sale shall be enjoyed or borne by the buyer.

Article 24: Where, after the enterprise is sold, the buyer incorporates the assets of the purchased enterprise into its own enterprise or converts the purchased enterprise into a subordinate branch, the debts of the purchased enterprise shall be borne by the buyer, unless the seller and the buyer have otherwise agreed and the creditors have approved.

Article 25: Where, after the enterprise is sold, the buyer contributes the assets of the purchased enterprise as shares to form a new company with others, and the legal person status of the purchased enterprise is cancelled, the buyer shall bear civil liability for the debts of the purchased enterprise before the sale with all of its property, including its equity in the newly formed company.

Article 26: Where, after the enterprise is sold, the buyer re-registers the purchased enterprise as a new enterprise legal person, and the legal person status of the purchased enterprise is cancelled, the debts of the purchased enterprise before the sale shall be borne by the newly registered enterprise legal person, unless the seller and the buyer have otherwise agreed and the creditors have approved.

Article 27: Where, after an enterprise is sold, the cancellation registration of the enterprise legal person should have been handled but has not been handled, and a creditor sues the enterprise, the People's Court shall, based on the specific circumstances after the transfer of enterprise assets, inform the creditor to add a liable subject, and order the liable subject to bear civil liability.

Article 28: Where, when selling an enterprise, the seller publicly notifies creditors by reference to the relevant provisions of the Company Law. After the enterprise is sold, if a creditor sues the buyer for the debts of the original enterprise concealed or omitted by the seller, and if the creditor has reported the claim within the announcement period, the buyer may, after bearing civil liability, seek recourse from the seller. If the creditor has not reported the claim within the announcement period, the buyer shall not bear civil liability. The People's Court may inform the creditor to separately sue the seller.

Article 29: Where the act of selling an enterprise has the circumstances prescribed in Articles 538 and 539 of the Civil Code, and the creditor exercises the right of revocation within the statutory period, the People's Court shall support it.
VII. Merger of Enterprises

Article 30: An enterprise merger agreement shall take effect from the date of signature and seal by the parties. Where approval by the competent government department is required, the merger agreement shall take effect from the date of approval; without approval, the enterprise merger agreement shall not take effect. However, if the parties complete the approval procedures before the conclusion of the debate at first instance, the People's Court shall confirm that the merger agreement is valid.
Article 31: After an absorption merger of enterprises, the debts of the merged enterprise shall be borne by the merging party.
Article 32: After a consolidation merger of enterprises, the debts of the merged enterprise shall be borne by the enterprise legal person after the consolidation.

Article 33: Where, after an absorption merger or consolidation merger of enterprises, the merged enterprise should have handled but has not handled the cancellation of business registration, and a creditor sues the merged enterprise, the People's Court shall, based on the specific circumstances after the merger, inform the creditor to add a liable subject, and order the liable subject to bear civil liability.

Article 34: Where an enterprise is controlled by means of acquisition, the debts of the controlled enterprise shall still be borne by itself. However, if the controlling enterprise withdraws funds or evades debts, causing the controlled enterprise to be unable to repay its debts, the debts of the controlled enterprise shall be borne by the controlling enterprise.
VIII. Supplementary Provisions

Article 35: These Provisions shall come into force as of February 1, 2003. Where judicial interpretations concerning enterprise restructuring formulated by this Court before the coming into force of these Provisions are inconsistent with these Provisions, they shall no longer be applied.
